description: Da Vinci external interoperability scenario inventory. This is the source of truth for which scenarios exist; execution status comes from a harness run, never from this file. A scenario listed here with no result in a run is reported NotRun.

scenarios.title: PAS $submit against the HL7 Da Vinci burden-reduction payer RI
scenarios.description: CHO's harness submits a synthetic PAS request bundle to the independent payer RI's Claim/$submit and parses/validates the PAS response bundle with the same FHIR parser CHO uses.

scenarios.title: CRD CDS Hooks exchange with the HL7 Da Vinci burden-reduction payer RI
scenarios.description: CHO acts as the provider-side CRD client: it discovers the payer RI's CDS Hooks services, selects the order-sign CRD service from discovery, invokes it with synthetic draft orders, and validates the CDS Hooks response and the Da Vinci coverage-information determinations it carries.

scenarios.title: DTR $questionnaire-package chained from the payer's own CRD determination
scenarios.description: CHO acts as the provider-side DTR client: it enters from the payer's own CRD determination, takes the DTR questionnaire canonical the payer named, requests exactly that canonical from the payer's $questionnaire-package, and validates the returned package and its declared dependencies.

scenarios.title: PAS $inquire against the burden-reduction payer RI
scenarios.description: Inquire on a prior authorization previously established by BR-PAS-SUBMIT-001 and validate the returned Parameters/responseBundle set.

scenarios.title: Inferno DTR payer-server suite against CHO
scenarios.description: Run the davinci-dtr-test-kit dtr_payer_server suite with CHO's FHIR base as the suite input and map Inferno result statuses into InteropResult.

scenarios.title: Inferno PDex payer-server suite against CHO
scenarios.description: Run the davinci-pdex-test-kit pdex_payer_server suite with CHO's FHIR base as the suite input.

scenarios.title: Inferno US Core 3.1.1 server suite against CHO's Patient and Encounter groups
scenarios.description: Run the us-core-test-kit us_core_v311 groups that correspond to what CHO's CapabilityStatement claims, against the seeded interop-cho profile. Deliberately the named groups rather than the whole suite: US Core 3.1.1 covers roughly thirty clinical resource types and CHO is a payer that publishes almost none of them, so a whole-suite run would bury the Patient and Encounter verdicts under failures for resources CHO never claimed. Naming the groups says which claim is tested; it does not soften the verdict on those groups. US Core 3.1.1+ is the floor CMS-0057-F sets, and us_core_v610 is the natural second run.

scenarios.title: Inferno CARIN BB v2.0.0 server groups CHO claims to serve
scenarios.description: Run the carin-for-blue-button-test-kit c4bb_v200 (financial) groups against the seeded interop-cho profile: the CapabilityStatement, and the Patient, Coverage, ExplanationOfBenefit, Organization and Practitioner groups. The RelatedPerson group is not run because CHO publishes no RelatedPerson; the SMART launch group is not run because the harness supplies an already-issued token rather than driving a launch; and the visual inspection and attestation group is manual by construction. The kit's c4bb_v200devnonfinancial suite is NOT run at the current pin: it checks the superseded '-NonFinancial' canonicals from the April 2023 branch snapshot it bundles, while CHO declares the CARIN BB 2.2.0 '-Basis' profiles, so it could not match CHO's EOBs in either direction. See knownMismatches for inferno-c4bb in interop/versions.json.

scenarios.title: Inferno Plan-Net server suite against CHO's public Provider Directory
scenarios.description: Run the whole davinci-plan-net-test-kit server suite against the public Provider Directory the interop-cho profile publishes at /fhir/r4/directory/interop (G-36): the CapabilityStatement, and the Endpoint, InsurancePlan, OrganizationAffiliation, PractitionerRole, Practitioner, HealthcareService, Location, Network and Organization groups, each with its searches, chains, reverse chains, includes and revincludes. The whole suite rather than named groups, because CHO claims every Plan-Net resource type. Only url is supplied: the suite's OAuth input is optional and is left unset, because the directory is public and a run with a token would not prove that, and the suite finds instances with parameterless searches (its default) over what scripts/interop/seed-cho.mjs seeded. The kit is generated from Plan-Net 1.1.0 while CHO serves 1.2.0; see knownMismatches for inferno-plan-net in interop/versions.json.

scenarios.title: Inferno Bulk Data 2.0.0 Group and Patient export against CHO
scenarios.description: Run the bulk-data-test-kit bulk_data_v200 Group export and Patient export groups against the interop-cho profile with bulk export on (G-60): kick-off, status polling, the manifest, downloading the NDJSON files with the token the manifest requires, validating the resources in them, cancel, and the outputFormat and _since parameters. group_id is the seeded billing provider, whose patients come from claims-history attribution. The kit authenticates itself with SMART Backend Services (private_key_jwt) against cho-smart-auth-service as a backend client the harness registers, bound to that provider, so the token, the provider binding and the export are all the real path. Not run: the server TLS group and the SMART Backend Services group, whose TLS checks cannot pass on the plain-HTTP interop network, and the system export group, because CHO does not serve system-level $export. See knownMismatches for inferno-bulk-data in interop/versions.json.

scenarios.title: Inferno PDex payer-client suite driven by CHO
scenarios.description: Run the davinci-pdex-test-kit pdex_payer_client suite with CHO acting as the payer client performing $member-match and clinical data retrieval.
